sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: HA-FcRL1(WT)-YFP/mCherry served as the functional wild-type control in BCR co-clustering, calcium flux, and tyrosine-phosphorylation signaling assays in primary B cells and CH27 cells; function was preserved relative to untagged FcRL1-KO rescue.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly states the HA tag is 'fused to the N terminus' of full-length FcRL1, and surface display on primary B cells was confirmed by FACS. Because the signal peptide spans residues 1–16 (computed landmarks), any N-terminal extracellular tag must be inserted after residue 16 (P) and before residue 17 (A, the mature N-terminus); this is the only possible extracellular N-terminal junction. Python confirmed residue 16 = P and residue 17 = A, and that position 17 lies 292 residues from the TM boundary (309), well clear of any steric constraint. The same junction is corroborated by independent FLAG-tagged FCRL1 constructs in L6/L7 and L8/L9. Full-length FcRL1 with HA fused to the N-terminus and YFP/mCherry to the C-terminus (HA-FcRL1(WT)-YFP/mCherry) was stably expressed on the surface of FcRL1-KO primary B cells and CH27 cells via lentiviral transduction; surface display confirmed by FACS. The paper names 'N terminus' but no residue number; the signal peptide (residues 1–16) is the only N-terminal feature, so the tag must land after residue 16 (the sole extracellular N-terminal junction). The same N-terminal position is independently supported by N-terminal FLAG-tagged FCRL1 constructs in two additional papers (L6/L7, L8/L9), all confirmed by anti-FLAG surface staining on non-permeabilized cells.

sources.claim: The distribution of FcRL1 molecules was visualized by expressing the HA-FcRL1-YFP chimera receptor with the hemagglutinin (HA) tag fused to the N terminus and yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) to the C terminus of FcRL1 on the surface of FcRL1-KO primary B cells.

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines converge on a single extracellular tag site: the N-terminal junction after the signal peptide (residue 16/17). L1–L5 (PMC6637015) report HA at the N-terminus; L6–L7 (PMC8629370) and L8–L9 (PMC3634363) independently report FLAG at the N-terminus, all with surface-display confirmation. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any internal extracellular loop of FCRL1. The tyrosine-mutant constructs in L2 (Y281F, Y293F, Y339F) are point mutations used to probe ITAM-like signaling motifs, not tag insertions, so they do not qualify as insertion sites. The C-terminal YFP/mCherry fusion (L1–L5) is placed in other_positions because residue 429 falls in the intracellular domain (330–429).

literature_other_positions.note: YFP or mCherry fused to the C-terminus of full-length FcRL1 in HA-FcRL1(WT)-YFP/mCherry constructs; residue 429 (M) is the last residue of the intracellular domain (330–429), so this fusion is cytoplasmic and not accessible for extracellular epitope tagging.
